abstract: Stanford/MIT study examining how AI tools affect accountant productivity and task allocation. In a sample of 277 accountants, AI assistance led to a 55% improvement in client support capabilities and an 8.5% reallocation of time from routine tasks to higher-value advisory work. The findings suggest AI augments rather than replaces accounting professionals, enabling them to shift toward more strategic, client-facing activities.
keyFindings: AI tools improved client support performance by 55% among participating accountants
8.5% of work time was reallocated from routine tasks to higher-value advisory activities
AI augmentation enabled accountants to handle more complex client queries without additional staffing
Benefits were most pronounced for mid-career professionals with established domain expertise
methodology: Field experiment with n=277 accountants at professional services firms, comparing task allocation and client support metrics before and after AI tool deployment. Stanford/MIT collaboration measuring productivity and time-use changes.
qualifiers: Sample limited to 277 accountants at firms that voluntarily adopted AI tools, introducing potential selection bias. Short observation window may not capture longer-term adjustment effects. Results may not generalize to smaller firms or solo practitioners.
